items.video_description:
DAIHATSU MIRA ES THE FIRST 660CC JDM KEI CAR CAME WITH DIGITAL METER AND CVT GEAR BOX IN 2011

The 2011 Daihatsu Mira e:S (e:S stands for "Eco Super") key features focus on extreme fuel efficiency, achieved through a lightweight body, aerodynamic design, and the world's first petrol CVT with an "Eco Idle" stop system, delivering around 30 km/L in JC08 mode, plus smart packaging and accessible tech like optional VSC and TAF safety. It's a 660cc, FWD mini-vehicle with CVT automatic transmission, DOHC engine, and practical elements like ample storage and available digital displays. 

The Daihatsu Mira has a fuel average of 18  in the city and on the highway. With a tank capacity of 36 L, it delivers an estimated driving range of 648 km approx 

Mira 2011 price in Pakistan ranges from PKR 1,550,000 to PKR 2,385,000

Fuel Efficiency & Eco Features

Eco Idle: Standard on all models, automatically stops the engine at speeds below 7 km/h to save fuel, a world-first for petrol CVTs.

Lightweight Design: Achieved by using thinner steel panels and resin parts in the body, reducing weight by about 60kg.

Aerodynamics: Improved shape, underbody panels, and low-rolling resistance tires reduced drag and rolling resistance.

Engine Tech: Optimized 660cc engine with low-friction parts and improved fuel injection. 

Performance & Drivetrain

Engine: 658cc, 3-cylinder, DOHC.

Transmission: Automatic (CVT).

Drivetrain: Front-Wheel Drive (FWD).

Power: Around 48-49 HP. 

Interior & Technology

Smart Packaging: Clever interior design for a spacious feel in a small car.

Eco Driving Assist: Expanded lights to help drivers recognize eco-driving.

Information Displays: TFT multi-information displays on higher trims show fuel efficiency and maintenance data.

Convenience: Plentiful storage, power windows, available keyless entry, and even an electric hatch opener on some later models (though maybe not 2011). 

Safety

TAF Body: Total Advance Function body for collision safety.

Safety Features: Available SRS side airbags and Vehicle Stability Control (VSC). 

The Daihatsu Mira generally offers better features, comfort, and fuel economy (especially older models), feeling more refined with a smooth CVT, while the locally sold Suzuki Alto provides peace of mind with easier maintenance, strong resale, and better parts availability, making it ideal for hassle-free ownership, though with lower interior quality and features. Choose Mira for a better driving experience, Alto for practical ownership in markets like Pakistan. 

Choose Daihatsu Mira if:

Comfort & Features: You prioritize better build quality, more advanced features (like push-start, climate control in higher trims), and a smoother ride. 

Fuel Efficiency: Older Mira models often boast excellent mileage (e.g., 33 km/L city). 

Automatic Transmission: It consistently comes with a smooth automatic (CVT). 

Choose Suzuki Alto if:

Ease of Ownership: You want easy access to parts, lower maintenance costs, and quick resale. 

New Car Peace of Mind: Buying new offers reliability and support. 

Budget-Friendly: A new Alto is often more accessible and manageable for beginners. 

Key Differences:

Build & Interior: Mira feels more solid and refined; Alto's local interior plastic quality can be a drawback. 

Maintenance: Alto wins for easy, cheap parts; Mira's parts can be harder/costlier. 

Fuel Economy: Varies, but some Miras beat Alto, though newer Altos are also efficient. 

Availability: Alto is locally assembled (new); Mira is a used Japanese import in many markets. 

Verdict: The Mira offers a superior driving experience for those who can manage potential parts challenges, while the Alto is the practical, worry-free choice for easy ownership and resale.
